messages:
devin_k: Heads-up: Customer AcmePay on Dedicated is asking for updated batching config. Current continuous-batcher is hitting the token budget cap and causing headroom loss for large chat requests. Need a proposal for token_budget_per_batch + max_queue_ms + per-request limits. Anyone on perf side?

maria_s: On it. Do we have profiler traces? I noticed increased kernel-selection thrash last week after the KV cache fix.

perf-bot: Profiling summary for pool 'acmepay-dedicated' (last 24h): p50 latency +12%, p95 +18%. KV cache hit-rate dropped 0.73 -> 0.62 for sessions >2k tokens. continuous-batcher avg batch_size=3.2 reqs, avg_tokens_per_batch=182.

samir: KV cache regression likely from LRU eviction threshold change (PR#4821). Evictions are firing earlier for >4k contexts which forces re-decoding and triggers fallback kernel paths (no KV reuse).

kevin_ops: Their SLA: p50 <= 200ms, p95 <= 750ms. They're on gpt-x-16q (quant). High token bursts from long chats. Proposed quick config: token_budget_per_batch=1024, max_queue_ms=60, max_concurrent_batches=8. Thoughts?

maria_s: 1024 might push the runtime to choose large-sequence kernels that are inefficient for small batches. Alternative: token_budget=512 + enable prefix-sticky-KV for sessions that exceed 2k tokens to keep cache locality.

devin_k: Can we make it dynamic? e.g. token_budget_target = min(1024, 4 * avg_req_tokens) and queue_timeout_ms = clamp(30, avg_latency_target/2, 120) so short sessions don't balloon batch tokens.

samir: I can add kernel-selection histograms per pool. Note: if token_budget hits 1024, kernel selector will often pick large-seq kernels which increase per-token latency for small batch sizes. We should also add per_req_token_limit=256 to avoid 'large kernel for small batch' regressions.

kevin_ops: Draft payload to share with customer (plain text):
```
{
  "token_budget_target": "min(1024, 4 * avg_req_tokens)",
  "per_req_token_limit": "256",
  "max_queue_ms": "60",
  "max_batch_size": "64",
  "enable_prefix_sticky_kv": "true",
  "rollback_condition": "p95 latency > +10% vs baseline"
}
```

maria_s: I'll spin up a short A/B on the pool: baseline vs proposed with sticky_kv + per_req_token_limit. Will compare p50/p95, tokens_per_batch distribution, kernel_switch counts. ETA ~3h.

devin_k: @samir can you add counters for runtime.kernel_switches and runtime.kv_evictions scoped to pools/acmepay so we can validate?

samir: Done. Metrics added: runtime.kernel_switches, runtime.kv_evictions. They appear in console under pools/acmepay within ~5m. Also added a per-pool histogram runtime.batch_token_dist.

perf-bot: A/B job started: job_id=ab-20260302-17. Monitoring p50/p95, kernel_switches, kv_evictions, tokens_per_batch. Will post results here when complete.

kevin_ops: :thumbsup: I'll draft the customer-facing email with the config and rollback plan. If p95 worsens >10% we auto-roll back to token_budget=512.

devin_k: Thanks team. Keep replies in-thread. We'll snapshot kernel histograms and attach them to the customer ticket (TICK-1428). If A/B shows improved kv hit-rate and stable p95, we can apply to production pool next maintenance window.

maria_s: Quick note — I'll also log the exact PR ids and kernel-version used in the A/B to help root-cause. PRs: #4821 (kv eviction tweak), #4879 (kernel selector tweak).

kevin_ops: Added customer note: "Expect intermittent higher p50 during rollout while kernels warm; p95 is the critical metric for us."

devin_k: Closing loop: once A/B finishes, we'll paste the brief perf summary (p50/p95 delta, kernel_switches delta, kv_hit delta) and send to AcmePay.

perf-bot: A/B progress: 12/12 windows completed, aggregating results...
